identity.name: Mamluk Iraq
alt_names: Mamluk pashaliks of Baghdad, Basra and Shahrizor

land.text: the Ottoman pashalik of Baghdad, to which Basra came 'from around 1705' (Ottoman Iraq page); the Baghdad, Basra, Mosul and Shahrizor eyalets had been separate Ottoman units

predecessors.note: Hasan Pasha was 'the Ottoman governor of Georgian origin sent from Constantinople' (Mamluk dynasty page). Cliopatria has no Mamluk Iraq row; the Ottoman Empire shape covers the land.

land.text: Baghdad, Basra and Shahrizor, 'brought under direct Ottoman rule' after Dawud Pasha's dismissal in 1831 (Ottoman Iraq page)

successors.note: Ali Rıza Pasha's army 'marched from Aleppo into Iraq' in 1831; Baghdad 'capitulated after a ten-week blockade'. Mosul stayed under the Jalili until 1834.

capitals.name: Baghdad
capitals.note: The Mamluk pashas were the governors of Baghdad ('pashaliks of Baghdad, Basrah, and Shahrizor'); the infobox capital is not stated on the page, so Baghdad is the researcher's reading.

rulers.name: Sulayman Abu Layla (son-in-law of Ahmad)
rulers.title: Pasha of Baghdad
rulers.note: The page does not explain the gap 1747-1749; 'the Porte recognized' him as the first Mamluk Pasha of Iraq by about 1750.

rulers.name: Sulayman the Great (son of Omar)
rulers.title: Pasha of Baghdad
rulers.note: Gap 1777-1780 on the page; he 'acquired the governorship of Baghdad, Basrah, and Shahrizor in 1780'.

rulers.name: Sulayman the Little (son of Sulayman the Great)
rulers.title: Pasha of Baghdad

rulers.name: Said Pasha (son of Sulayman the Great)
rulers.title: Pasha of Baghdad

rulers.name: Dawud Pasha
rulers.title: Pasha of Baghdad
rulers.note: Dismissed by the sultan in 1830; Baghdad fell to Ali Rıza Pasha in 1831.

correction.text: the pashalik of Baghdad: central Iraq from the Euphrates and Diyala to the Tigris below Tikrit, without Basra, Shahrizor and Mosul

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks a Mamluk Iraq row). 'Such Mamluks presided over Iraq from 1704 to 1831' (infobox); Hasan Pasha 1704-1723. The Ottoman Iraq page instead dates the Mamluk period 1749-1831 (see notes). The pages give no infobox area ('page silent'); the shape is about 243,000 km2 by cells, soft desert edge.

correction.text: the pashaliks of Baghdad and Basra: central and southern Iraq. 'Basra came under Baghdad's control from around 1705'; Mosul was Jalili and Shahrizor (Kirkuk, Erbil, Sulaymaniyah) not yet under Baghdad

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, about 343,000 km2 by cells with the Iraqi desert west of the Euphrates (soft edge; no infobox area on the pages). The Mamluk dynasty page says Sulayman Abu Layla 'brought Basra under their control' without a year, after 1749, against 'around 1705' on the Ottoman Iraq page; this dossier follows the dated statement.

correction.text: Baghdad and Basra's hinterland without the city of Basra and its governorate, held by the Zands: 'Sadeq Khan entered the city the following day' (21 April 1776)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1776-1778 (the Zands 'established a local administration that lasted until the death of Karim Khan Zand in 1779'). Muntafiq lands north-west of Basra stayed Ottoman-aligned; the page does not map them, so only the Basra governorate is removed.

correction.text: Basra back with Baghdad after the Zand withdrawal following Karim Khan's death in 1779

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1779 only. The siege page says the Zands withdrew in 1779 but its account of the recapture ('Soleyman Aqa was able to recapture the city') is unclear; the Mamluk dynasty page has Sulayman the Great governing Baghdad, Basra and Shahrizor from 1780.

correction.text: the pashaliks of Baghdad, Basrah and Shahrizor: 'Sulayman the Great acquired the governorship of Baghdad, Basrah, and Shahrizor in 1780'; Mosul remained the Jalili's

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, about 385,000 km2 by cells counting all of Iraq's central and southern provinces plus Kirkuk, Erbil and Sulaymaniyah (no infobox area given). Sulaymaniyah is contested with Iran from 1818 (ledger); the Ottoman Iraq page says Mosul and Shahrizor 'followed after 1780' in the consolidation, but gives Mosul as Jalili until 1834.

ledger.note: 1704: Hasan Pasha begins the Mamluk line at Baghdad. 'Such Mamluks presided over Iraq from 1704 to 1831'; Hassan Pasha, 'the Ottoman governor of Georgian origin sent from Constantinople', governs 1704-1723.

region.text: the Basra eyalet: Basra, Dhi Qar, Maysan and Muthanna in the south

ledger.note: c. 1705: Basra comes under Baghdad's control. The Ottoman Iraq page: 'Basra came under Baghdad's control from around 1705'; the Mamluk dynasty page has Sulayman Abu Layla 'brought Basra under their control' with no year.

region.text: the city of Basra, held by Soleyman Aqa 'subordinate to the Mamluk rulers of Iraq'

ledger.note: 20 April 1776: Basra falls to the Zands. The garrison 'surrendered on 20 April 1776' after a siege begun 6 April 1775 and 'Sadeq Khan entered the city the following day'; Omar Pasha of Baghdad 'provided limited to no support'.

region.text: the city and governorate of Basra

ledger.note: 1779: Basra returns to Baghdad. The Zands 'withdrew in 1779' on Karim Khan's death after a 6,000-man garrison; the page's account of the Ottoman recapture is unclear, and the Mamluk page has Sulayman the Great in charge of Basra from 1780.

region.text: the pashalik of Shahrizor: Kirkuk, Erbil and Sulaymaniyah

ledger.note: 1780: Sulayman the Great adds Shahrizor. 'Sulayman the Great acquired the governorship of Baghdad, Basrah, and Shahrizor in 1780'; the Ottoman Iraq page: Mosul and Shahrizor 'followed after 1780' (Mosul stayed Jalili).

region.text: Sulaymaniyah and the Baban lands of Shahrizor

ledger.note: 1818: Iran occupies Sulaymaniyah. The Mamluk dynasty page: Sulaymaniyah 'occupied by Iran in 1818' under Dawud Pasha; the Ottoman-Persian War page puts Mohammad-Ali Mirza's conquest of Sulaymaniyah and Shahrezur and the siege of Baghdad in the 1821-1823 war without a year.

28 July 1823: the Treaty of Erzurum restores the old frontier. 'Both sides recognized the previous borders established by the Treaty of Zuhab in 1639', 'no territorial changes'; Sulaymaniyah and Shahrezur stay with Baghdad.

1831: the sultan's army marches on Baghdad. 'In 1830 the Sultan decreed Dawud Pasha's dismissal' but the emissary was executed in Baghdad; in 1831 'the Ottoman army under Ali Riza Pasha marched from Aleppo into Iraq' (the page gives no month).
1831: Baghdad capitulates. 'Baghdad capitulated after a ten-week blockade'; Dawud Pasha surrendered (the Ottoman Iraq page adds plague weakened his forces); the page gives no month.

region.text: the pashaliks of Baghdad, Basra and Shahrizor passed to direct Ottoman governors

ledger.note: 1831: Mamluk rule in Iraq ends. 'Ali Ridha Pasha, the new Ottoman governor, arrived in 1831 and marked the start of direct Ottoman rule'; 'Baghdad was brought under direct Ottoman rule' (Ottoman Iraq page); Dawud Pasha exiled to Bursa, 'died in 1851'.

wars.name: Persian attack on Iraq of 1733
wars.outcome: Nader Shah's forces attacked Erbil and Kirkuk; Topal Osman Pasha defeated them near Baghdad but was killed near Kirkuk and Kirkuk capitulated; Mosul's governor repelled a six-day siege. Ahmed Pasha of Baghdad 'withdrew during the 1733 fighting, citing a lack of provisions'.
wars.note: The zone (Erbil, Kirkuk) was Shahrizor, not Baghdad's before 1780, and the page records no lasting change; zones left empty. The 1743 siege of Baghdad is not on the page.

wars.name: Siege of Basra (1775-1776)
wars.outcome: Sadeq Khan Zand besieged Basra from 6 April 1775; the Ottoman garrison surrendered on 20 April 1776. The Zands held it until the death of Karim Khan in 1779, with a 6,000-man garrison.
wars.note: Omar Pasha of Baghdad 'sent a letter to Oman requesting naval support' but gave 'limited to no support'; the Muntafiq 'took little action'.

wars.name: Wahhabi raids on Najaf and Hillah
wars.outcome: Ali al-Kahiya 'repelled raids on Najaf and Hillah' in 1803 and 1806 but 'failed to challenge their domination of the desert'.
wars.note: No border change recorded on the page; the desert edge of the shape stays soft.

wars.name: Ottoman-Persian War (1821-1823)
wars.outcome: Dawud Pasha invaded Iran and failed; Mohammad-Ali Mirza 'took Shahrezur, conquered Sulaymaniyah, and besieged Baghdad' until cholera lifted the siege. The Treaty of Erzurum, 28 July 1823, restored the 1639 Zuhab borders: 'no territorial changes'.
wars.note: The Mamluk dynasty page dates the Iranian occupation of Sulaymaniyah to 1818; this page gives no year for the Baghdad front.

wars.name: Ottoman campaign against Dawud Pasha
wars.outcome: The sultan decreed Dawud's dismissal in 1830; his emissary was executed; Ali Riza Pasha marched from Aleppo in 1831 and Baghdad capitulated after a ten-week blockade. Direct Ottoman rule followed.
wars.note: The page spells the commander both Ali Riza and Ali Ridha Pasha and gives no month.

certainty.note: The Iraqi desert west of the Euphrates, the Kurdish hills and the Muntafiq marshes are approximate. The Iranian frontier follows the Treaty of Zuhab line of 1639, 'recognized' again on 28 July 1823, but was never surveyed in the pages opened. Mosul (Jalili) is outside the shape.

sources.title: Mamluk dynasty (Iraq)
sources.note: Identity, 1704-1831, the list of pashas, the territories (Baghdad, Basrah, Shahrizor in 1780), Sulaymaniyah 1818, Wahhabi raids 1803/1806, the 1830-31 end. Page silent on capital, area and months.

sources.title: Ottoman Iraq
sources.note: Basra under Baghdad from around 1705; Mosul/Shahrizor after 1780; Mosul Jalili to 1834; 1733 Nader Shah; the four eyalets; direct rule 1831; page dates the Mamluk period 1749-1831.

sources.title: Siege of Basra (1775-1776)
sources.note: 6 April 1775 to 20 April 1776; Zand administration to 1779; Omar Pasha of Baghdad gives little support.

sources.title: Dawud Pasha
sources.note: A disambiguation page: only the line that Dawud Pasha of Baghdad (d. 1851) was the last Mamluk ruler of Iraq. Thin.

sources.title: Ottoman-Persian War (1821-1823)
sources.note: Persian invasion 1821, the Baghdad front, Treaty of Erzurum 28 July 1823 restoring the Zuhab borders.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (the Ottoman Empire shape covers it); new dossier by me-10-x. Start year: the Mamluk dynasty page says 1704-1831 (Hasan Pasha 1704-1723), while the Ottoman Iraq page dates the Mamluk period 1749-1831; this dossier follows 1704. Basra: 'around 1705' (Ottoman Iraq) against Sulayman Abu Layla's undated annexation (Mamluk page). Counterparts needing dossiers: the Jalili dynasty of Mosul (1726-1834, autonomous, not Mamluk); the Baban emirate of Sulaymaniyah (Shahrizor); the Muntafiq confederation (page silent 1704-1831). The ottoman-empire dossier could record the Mamluk pashaliks as an autonomous vassal (vassal_start with counterpart mamluk-iraq, c. 1750 per 'the Porte recognized' Sulayman Abu Layla); this dossier holds no vassal event because the suzerain records it. The Dawud Pasha Wikipedia title is a disambiguation page (thin); the 1831 month is not on any page opened. Baghdad capital is the researcher's reading (infobox silent). Admin-1 names used are Natural Earth spellings (Al-Basrah, Dhi-Qar, As-Sulaymaniyah, At-Ta'mim, Sala ad-Din, Karbala').
